title: surgical fallback runbook for config apply with KV-cache quarantine and cost-aware rollback advisor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a surgical, route-scoped fallback and runbook that quarantines affected KV-cache prefixes when a config change (batching/buffering/cache/quantization) causes regressed latency or token cost. Goal: avoid noisy global rollbacks by isolating impact, automatically fall back to a safe serving profile for affected routes, and provide human-in-the-loop rollback suggestions that are cost-aware.
background: We frequently need to update serving config (batch windows, cache eviction, kernel hints, quantization flags). Broad rollbacks are safe but expensive and disruptive. Existing rollback flows are global and often result in customer-visible outages or unnecessary capacity churn. This ticket proposes a surgical quarantine flow that isolates cache and batching changes to affected route keys, monitors a fixed set of metrics, and provides an automated advisor that recommends either (a) targeted revert for the affected route, (b) staged canary adjustments, or (c) manual review with rollback playbook. The advisor factors in cost delta, request fanout, and SLO risk.
technical_design:
High-level design:
- Change detector: subscribe to config-apply events and compute delta against previous profile.
- Impact surface analyzer: map config delta to route prefixes, model variants, and KV-cache namespaces.
- Quarantine action: for affected prefixes, spawn 'quarantine mode' which splits traffic (primary vs fallback) at reverse-proxy/router level for 5% live shadow by default. Quarantine mode also pins a duplicate serving process with previous cache behavior for comparison.
- Metric collector: collect route-scoped metrics (cache-hit-ratio, kv-miss-rate, token-cost-per-request, p50/p95 latency, error-rate) in rolling 60s windows.
- Trigger rules: cost-aware hysteresis rules (see metrics_and_triggers) to decide automatic fallback or advisor alert.
- Fallback execution: either toggle route to previous stable config (fast path) or shift to compatibility profile (slightly degraded but safe) with controlled ramp down.
- Advisor engine: simulate 1-hour cost projection and recommend action with expected delta. Outputs human-readable rationale and confidence score.
- Reconciliation controller: ensure eventual state convergence, prevent flip-flop by applying cooldown and token-bucket based guardrail.
- Observability: runbook dashboard, diff view of config before/after, and one-click rollback with audit trail.
Implementation notes:
- Keep quarantine state small: only store metadata for prefixes (TTL 24h).
- Use existing routing hooks in gateway-service; avoid global route table changes.
- Preference for read-only experiments first: shadow traffic -> warm caches -> then partial cutover.
- All changes must emit structured events to /events/config-safety for later analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine can be triggered automatically for a route prefix when defined triggers fire
Fallback executes within the SLO-defined timeout (default: 12s) and reduces observed regression within one evaluation window
Advisor provides an action recommendation with simulated cost delta and confidence score in >95% of test cases
Runbook page with step-by-step rollback instructions and one-click rollback link is available in Console for affected route
Reconciliation controller prevents flip-flop by enforcing cooldown and records action in audit logs
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag behind config-safety.quarantine. 2) Internal canary: enable on dev and staging services for 2 weeks. 3) Beta: enable for 5 low-traffic customer routes with on-call present. 4) Gradual ramp: increase eligible prefixes by 2x per day while monitoring SLOs. 5) Full opt-in: make available to Dedicated customers and self-serve in Console.
Fallback: global rollback remains available as emergency stop; runbook documents when to use it.
testing_plan: Unit tests for change-detector and advisor simulation; integration tests for quarantine lifecycle (enter, monitor, fallback, reconcile); chaos tests simulating increased token cost and cache degeneration; synthetic workload regressions using loadgen with varying sequence lengths. Test harness links: https://gitlab.redwood-inference/tests/quarantine-harness. Include canary dashboards and alert rules before enabling on production.
metrics_and_triggers: Primary metrics: cache-hit-ratio (route), kv-miss-rate, token-cost-per-request, p95 latency, error-rate
Automatic quarantine trigger: >=3 windows of 60s where (token-cost-per-request increases by >=15% AND p95 latency increases by >=10%)
Advisor automatic fallback trigger: 2 consecutive windows where cost increases by >=25% OR error-rate increases by >=1% absolute
Hysteresis rule: require rollback condition to hold for 3 of 5 consecutive evaluation windows to avoid transient flips
Cost guardrail: if projected 1-hour cost delta >20% AND impacted QPS > 1000, prefer advisor-only alert and wait for manual approval

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives trigger unnecessary quarantines -> Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and 5% shadowing before any cutover
Risk: Quarantine causes performance overhead -> Mitigation: keep quarantine lightweight metadata, avoid full duplication unless necessary
Risk: Flip-flop where config alternates between states -> Mitigation: cooldown and token-bucket guardrails plus reconcile controller
Risk: Advisor gives incorrect cost projection -> Mitigation: run historical backtests on last 6 months and build confidence scoring
Risk: Partial quarantine leaks to metrics pipelines -> Mitigation: tag metrics with quarantine context and filter in dashboards
